title: RAG with LlamaIndex .NET
description: Implement RAG using LlamaIndex-style indexing, retrieval, and query pipelines in C#.

blocks.text: LlamaIndex is known for data-focused RAG primitives. In the .NET ecosystem, you can adopt similar patterns or use the .NET client where available. This lesson focuses on concepts that translate across languages: indexes, nodes, retrievers, and query engines.

blocks.title: LlamaIndex concepts and .NET equivalents
items: **Nodes** — smaller units derived from documents for retrieval.
**Index** — a retrieval structure built from nodes and embeddings.
**Retriever** — fetches relevant nodes for a query.
**Query engine** — combines retrieval and generation into one call.

blocks.title: Focus on patterns
blocks.text: If the .NET client is still evolving, implement the same patterns using plain C# abstractions. The architecture matters more than the exact package.

blocks.title: Build a LlamaIndex-Style RAG Service
blocks.description: Create a small service that indexes documents and answers questions using retrieval.
steps: Choose documents and define node splitting logic.
Build an index with embeddings and metadata.
Implement a retriever that filters by metadata before ranking.
Create a query method that returns cited answers.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should have a working retrieval pipeline with clear separation between indexing, retrieval, and generation.
